holidays.name: National Chop Suey Day
holidays.description: A salute to the saucy, stir-fried medley of meat, crisp vegetables and gravy that became a staple of Chinese-American takeout. Grab your chopsticks and your favorite white takeout box.
holidays.origin: The dish traces back to tsap seui, meaning 'miscellaneous pieces,' from Taishan in Guangdong, China. It was popularized in the United States in the late 1800s and grew into a Chinese-American classic.
holidays.funFact: The name roughly means 'odds and ends,' which makes chop suey one of the original clean-out-the-fridge dinners.

holidays.name: National Lemon Juice Day
holidays.description: A zesty day for squeezing the most out of lemons. They go into lemonade and salad dressings, and people also use them for cleaning and home remedies.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is separate from National Lemon Day, which falls on July 23.
holidays.funFact: Lemon juice is acidic enough to keep sliced apples and avocados from browning, so one squeeze can save a snack.

holidays.name: Potteries Bottle Oven Day
holidays.description: This is a nod to the towering, bottle-shaped brick kilns that once filled the skyline of Stoke-on-Trent, England. They fired the region's famous pottery. The day honors the end of an industrial era.
holidays.origin: It marks the last coal firing of a traditional bottle oven in the Potteries, which happened on August 29, 1978.
holidays.funFact: Stoke-on-Trent once had thousands of these bottle kilns, and only a small number survive today as protected landmarks.
